name: Game (definition)
oneLine: A repeating sequence of ulterior transactions, hooking a hidden weak spot, that ends in a Switch and a Payoff of racket feeling - not just any conflict.
whatYouDid: You diagnosed Theo's "I'll pay you back" pattern against pastime, operation, and manoeuvre, and found the piece that makes it a game: the Switch and the repeating Payoff, not just the bad feeling.
confusion: People call any argument or conflict "a game"; the tell is structure, not unpleasantness - a one-off bad conversation is not a game, and a very polite, friendly exchange can be one if it has an ulterior Con, a Switch, and a Payoff.

fromBook.quote: Games are played without Adult awareness.

expand.definition: Berne's later definition requires Formula G in full: an ulterior transaction that hooks a Gimmick, runs a Response, pulls a Switch, causes a Crossup, and lands a Payoff of racket feeling - miss the Switch, and it's racketeering, not a game.
expand.otherFraming: Vann Joines' plain-language version: a game is doing something with an ulterior motive that stays outside Adult awareness, doesn't become explicit until the participants switch, and leaves everyone confused and wanting to blame someone.
expand.tryThisToday: Next time an interaction ends with you blindsided and thinking "how did that happen again," rewind and look for the Switch - the moment just before the confusion is where the real game was.
